transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. I'm Heidi, and I'm here because I just don’t feel any interest in the community projects and hobbies that used to mean everything to me. I used to be so active with my walking tours, church, and senior center, but now I just can't bring myself to care or participate anymore.
Have you felt this persistent loss of interest for most of the last two years, or is this a more recent change that started in the last few weeks or months?

No, it's not a recent change; it has been dragging on for over two years now. It started shortly after that terrible accident at the crosswalk when the truck hit those kids, and I just haven't been able to find my way back to myself since.
During these past two years, have you experienced any periods of feeling relatively 'normal' or symptom-free for more than two months at a time?
No, I haven't had any breaks or times where I felt like my old self. It has been a continuous, heavy cloud hanging over me for the entire two years without ever letting up.
During these past two years, have you experienced other symptoms like changes in your appetite, sleep patterns, energy levels, or feelings of worthlessness?

I haven't really noticed any major changes in my appetite or energy levels. I do have a lot of trouble winding down at night when those memories keep me awake, but I'm not really sure about the other symptoms you mentioned.
When you are awake at night, do you find yourself having intrusive, distressing memories or flashbacks of the accident that make you feel as if the event is happening all over again?

Yes, especially at night when everything is quiet, I get pulled right back to that corner and see that poor boy get hit all over again. I hear the thud and the screaming so vividly that my body shakes and I feel physically sick, as if I'm standing right there in the chaos.
Do you go out of your way to avoid that specific street corner or any other reminders of the accident, and do you feel like you are constantly on edge or easily startled since that day?

Yes, I take the long way around town just to avoid that intersection, and I completely shut down if anyone even mentions car accidents. I'm also constantly on edge, obsessively watching traffic before I step off the curb and tensing up at every loud engine rev. When I'm in a café, I have to face the door just so I can keep an eye on everything and feel safe.
Since the accident, have you felt that your low mood and lack of interest are specifically tied to these recurring memories and your efforts to avoid reminders of the event?

Yes, they are deeply connected. Constantly trying to avoid that intersection and fighting off those terrifying, vivid memories of the crash leaves me completely drained. Living in that constant state of dread and exhaustion makes it feel impossible to find any energy or genuine interest for the hobbies and people I used to love.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits hallmark symptoms of Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD), including re-experiencing (flashbacks, intrusive memories), persistent avoidance (avoiding the intersection, shutting down), and hyperarousal (hypervigilance, startle response). These symptoms have persisted for over two years following a traumatic event and are the primary driver of her functional impairment and loss of interest in activities.
